title: RBCBF: Decoding Time Safety Alignment via Risk Guided Rollback and Barrier Control
claim: Heuristic rollback blindly retries and loops on unsafe output; ours localizes decisive prefixes and applies targeted constrained repair.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, blue vs. red, token strips and risk-curve inset
description: Two side-by-side panels. The left, blue panel (a) is labeled 'Heuristic rollback'. It has a rule box showing strips of gray tokens with 'regenerate every N steps' and 'supervised signals'. Below it a trajectory shows an attack prompt, with rows of gray tokens ending in red unsafe tokens, a shield risk detector, and speech bubbles ('Seems bad, need to regenerate', 'Oops, bad again', 'Again, keep looping'). A legend lists the token and icon meanings. The right, pink panel (b) is labeled 'Ours: RBCBF'. A three-step flow reads 'Formulate why risk accumulated', 'Find the dominant rollback step', 'Apply constraint, fix the bad tokens'. Below it, a single token row turns red tokens into green corrected ones. Three small risk-vs-time curves are annotated with t_u, t_* and a CBF correction. The caption 'Less try & safer response' closes the panel. The eye goes first to the color contrast between the blue and pink panels.
caption: Overview of rollback-based inference-time interventions: (a) Heuristic or engineering rollback strategies that repeatedly retry without localizing decisive prefixes; (b) Rollback based on RBCBF that selects a small set of decisive prefixes and performs targeted repair.
abstract: Existing decoding-time safety interventions are often reactive, relying on local signals to correct unsafe outputs after they emerge. Under adversarial prompts that drive generation into recurring unsafe response, such local signals provide weak guidance for stable repair. As a result, rollback and post-hoc rewriting often trade-off response quality with recurrent violations. To address these limitations, we propose RBCBF, a rollback-based decoding-time framework that jointly selects intervention steps and performs distribution-level corrective control. Our key innovation is a risk-aggregation formulation that views terminal violations as the accumulated build-up of risk along the prefix. By selecting rollback steps from these decisive prefixes, RBCBF moves rollback targeting beyond heuristic cues and turns it into a trajectory-level decision. RBCBF then applies invasive corrective control to the next-token distribution under multiple rule constraints. Across jailbreak-style evaluations, RBCBF outperforms prior rollback methods and decoding-time baselines, reducing harmful responses and substantially lowering violation recurrence.
